claims.text: The feedstock is an AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder.
Optimized laser powder bed fusion with in-situ alloy formation will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention will produce AlCrFeNiSi components with relative density above 98%.
Laser powder bed fusion with in-situ alloy formation will form a single-phase solid solution in AlCrFeNiSi.
The intervention will produce a refined grain structure.
In-situ alloy formation from mixed feedstock is feasible during laser powder bed fusion.
Rapid solidification during laser powder bed fusion causes formation of the proposed single-phase, refined microstructure.
In-situ alloy formation and rapid solidification produce nonequilibrium chemical short-range order.
The single-phase, refined microstructure and chemical short-range order cause improved mechanical properties, reduced residual stress, and increased density.
A volumetric energy density window of 50 to 83 J/mm3 is applicable to the proposed AlCrFeNiSi process.
An applicable layer-thickness window is 20 to 50 micrometers.
An applicable scan-speed window is 100 to 500 mm/s.
Higher volumetric energy density creates a risk of titanium evaporation.
Optimizing volumetric energy density can minimize titanium evaporation while retaining the desired microstructure and properties.

contradictions.description: The stated AlCrFeNiSi alloy contains no titanium, yet the processing conditions and uncertainty focus on minimizing titanium evaporation. That concern was transferred from CrFeNiTi evidence and is incompatible with the named composition.
